page: Amazon Web Services g6e.16xlarge is a GPU-accelerated computing instance hosted on the AWS Nitro System. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with 64 vCPUs (32 physical cores and 2 threads per core) operating at a 3.4 GHz base clock on the x86_64 architecture. Memory provisioning is substantial, featuring 512.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, equating to 8.0 GB per vCPU. Acceleration is provided by a single dedicated NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPU equipped with 45 GB of VRAM. For fast local data access, the instance bundles 1900 GB of NVMe SSD storage alongside a 35 Gbps baseline network throughput.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel compute and machine learning execution. In LLM inference tests, the NVIDIA L40S GPU places g6e.16xlarge in the top tier (top 10%), achieving 13507.83 tokens per second for prompt processing on a small 135M model and 135.89 tokens per second for text generation on a medium 7B model. Even under a 70B parameter model, prompt processing reaches 883.0 tokens per second. Host compute remains consistently strong, with a multi-core stress-ng score of 95699.34 and a PassMark CPU score of 67139.35. Cached memory bandwidth delivers 4551.38 GB/sec, while in-memory Redis SET operations achieve 69.39 million operations per second.

Hardware tradeoffs emerge primarily between single-thread and multi-thread capabilities. While multi-threaded compute and extended matrix/vector tasks perform within the top 25%, single-core Geekbench scores (1693.0) and uncached memory bandwidth (123.8 GB/sec read and 61.91 GB/sec write) place in the middle 50% category. In terms of architectural flags, the AMD EPYC 7R13 supports standard AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA extensions, but lacks AVX-512 and AMX instruction sets.

Qualitatively, the server provides balanced hardware density by pairing high system memory (512 GB) and high-speed local NVMe storage with an enterprise Ada Lovelace GPU. This combination renders g6e.16xlarge well-aligned for large language model inference, real-time AI computer vision pipelines, multi-stream video transcoding, 3D graphics rendering, and memory-intensive GPU-backed database caching workloads.
description: Amazon Web Services g6e.16xlarge is an accelerated computing instance featuring an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor with 64 vCPUs (32 physical cores) clocked at 3.4 GHz, 512.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and a single NVIDIA Ada Lovelace L40S GPU with 45 GB VRAM. The platform includes 1900 GB of local NVMe SSD storage and 35 Gbps baseline networking on the Nitro hypervisor. Benchmarks confirm top-tier inference capability across 135M to 70B parameter language models, complemented by strong multi-core CPU metrics (PassMark 67139.35, multi-core stress-ng 95699.34) and high Redis throughput. Uncached memory bandwidth and single-core metrics sit in the middle 50% tier. This instance fits production LLM inference, 3D rendering, video encoding, and memory-heavy GPU computing tasks.
